Beginner: What does the word “training” describe when people say a text model learned from examples?
Adjusting the model's internal numbers using examples of text.
adjust/learn
example/text
A writer enters “The boat floated on the”. What is a completion?
A continuation of that unfinished text.
continuation/ending/next
What does inference mean when a trained model drafts an invitation?
Using the trained model to produce the draft.
using/running/applying
trained/model
In a toy choice between endings, which is more likely, 0.7 or 0.3?
0.7 has the larger chance.
What part of “park the car” helps establish the meaning of the word park?
The surrounding words “the car” supply context.
car/context
Intermediate: A piano teacher asks for three possible recital titles. What task characteristic makes sampling several endings useful?
Several creative titles can meet the request.
creative/several/variety
An order prompt states “six chairs.” A generated draft says “five.” What exact field failed?
The chair quantity changed from six to five.
quantity/count/number
A weather bot has no weather feed and a user asks for the temperature outside now. Which information would turn its draft into a checkable answer?
A current local weather observation.
current/live
local/weather
Advanced: A fictional writing exercise and a refund notice both demand confident prose. Which error would you weigh more heavily in the notice and why?
An unsupported refund promise can cause a real customer to rely on an incorrect policy.
A small model proposes ten product names. A larger model shares the same false claim about a trademark. What evidence is still missing?
Independent authoritative trademark information applicable to the proposed name.
You compare two models on completion accuracy and one always copies the input. What control cases would reveal that shortcut?
Include held-out prompts whose correct continuation differs from the supplied text.
A historical letter sounds perfectly authentic but includes a place opened years later. What test separates stylistic fit from factual consistency?
Check named places and dates against the historical timeline independently of style.
A draft contains a personally identifying phrase from a user's example. What observation shows copying in this run without proving memorization during training?
The phrase appears in the supplied context and reappears in the output.

Beginner: Why can one printed emoji require several model tokens?
The tokenizer can represent its encoded text using several pieces.
tokenizer/pieces/encoded
In the phrase “bring it back,” what counts as input when you send it to a model?
The supplied phrase and any other request instructions or context.
supplied/request/input/instructions
What is generated output in a question-and-answer exchange?
The text produced in the reply.
reply/response/produced
What does truncating a passage do?
It cuts off part of the passage.
cut/remove/shorten
Why does punctuation matter when counting model input?
Punctuation can contribute to tokenization and the token count.
token/piece/count
Intermediate: A shop assistant reserves 100 pieces for a reply and has 20 remaining after adding history. How much space must be recovered?
At least 80 pieces.
80/eighty
A model's tokenizer counts a plain address and its quoted JSON form differently. Which form should a budget calculation count?
Count the serialized form actually sent in the request.
actual/serialized/serialized form/sent
A chatbot blindly drops the first message to save space. That message held the customer's order number. Which fact should be retained for the current order?
The verified order number linked to this customer's current task.
order
number/id
Advanced: A budget tool counts only the document body, then actual requests overflow. Which items should a representative full-request measurement include?
Include system instructions, tool descriptions, conversation text, formatting overhead and the output allocation.
A 100-token answer limit fits checkout explanations but truncates code examples. What measurement would support task-specific limits?
Compare completion lengths and truncation rates separately by task, then set limits from those distributions.
A model changes its tokenizer while the app keeps cached counts for articles. Which key or invalidation should protect the budget?
Version cached counts by tokenizer and source-text revision, and invalidate incompatible counts.
A recent message says “use the earlier option.” After shortening the conversation, the earlier choice has vanished. How should a summary maintain the reference?
Preserve the actual option identifiers and decision context or ask the user to clarify.
Your system accepts a file with 200 pages before estimating prompt size. How could admission avoid wasting processing while keeping a final accurate bound?
Use a cheap preliminary size check, then measure exact tokens on the selected request before sending.

Beginner: Who specifies the task in a prompt asking “sort these letters by date”?
The person or application supplying the instruction.
person/user/application/instruction
In “answer with one sentence,” which property of the reply is constrained?
Its length or sentence count.
length/sentence
What is a delimiter around an input letter used to show?
Where the letter's content starts and ends.
starts/begins/boundary
ends/boundary
A brand message should sound courteous. What does tone describe?
The style or manner of expression.
style/manner
What is an input example in an instruction for extracting postcodes?
A sample address or note that contains a postcode to extract.
sample/example
address/note
Intermediate: A message-classification prompt has examples but never names the requested task. What simple addition would tell the model what to do?
State the classification task and required output explicitly.
task/classif
output/label
A shop asks for a two-sentence summary but needs the date and venue in every summary. How should the must-have content be expressed?
Specify both date and venue as required facts and define handling when either is missing.
date
venue
Two trial prompts use different examples and different scoring rules. What comparison would isolate the example change?
Keep the judging rule and test cases fixed while changing only the examples.
fixed/same
examples
Advanced: One proposed extraction instruction quietly replaces “no evidence” with a guessed default. What evaluation subset would reveal the damage?
Cases with deliberately missing evidence whose correct result is unknown or clarification.
A support workflow uses one prompt to select a tool and write a customer reply. A label error triggers an expensive action. How could you check the decision before acting?
Validate the structured action and authorization separately before running the tool or sending its reply.
A lengthy prompt contains two contradictory instructions about reply language. Which intervention makes behavior testable for multilingual inputs?
Resolve the priority rule explicitly and test examples for each supported language conflict.
A model copies sample customer names into unrelated summaries. What controlled test would separate literal copying from correct extraction?
Substitute different names in the input and examples independently and require output names to track the actual input.
A prompt revision changes defaults for missing quantities. How should existing customer workflows discover the semantic change?
Version and document the default rule and regression-test downstream behavior for incomplete orders.

Beginner: What is the client when a café tablet asks an online translation service for a result?
The tablet application making the request.
tablet/app
What is a response body?
The data the service returns inside its reply.
data/returned/content
A service returns an error code. What does the code communicate?
A category or status of the request outcome.
status/category/outcome
What is an endpoint in a service that offers translation and speech?
A named request address or operation for a particular service function.
address/operation/function
What does a request identifier help a support worker locate?
The records for one specific request.
request
record/trace/log
Intermediate: A school needs 300 translations before tomorrow, and pupils do not need immediate replies. What execution arrangement suits this workload?
Queue a bounded batch job and record per-item outcomes.
batch/queue
item/outcome
A provider returns an error for unsupported language code XY. Why will an unchanged retry usually fail?
The invalid parameter remains unchanged.
invalid/unsupported
parameter/language
A customer's phone disconnects after the service returns a translation to the server. Where could the app preserve a finished result for reconnection?
Save it on the application server under the authorized request identity.
server/storage
identity/request
Advanced: A translation form uses a 2-second client deadline and a 20-second provider deadline. Why can the server continue spending after the customer gives up?
The downstream operation may continue unless cancellation or a compatible deadline propagates.
A provider splits one answer into streaming pieces. The connection breaks halfway through. What should a durable result record distinguish?
Partial received text and a confirmed completed response must have different completion status.
You replace the provider and language quality falls only for short phrases. What paired comparison would distinguish malformed payloads from model weakness?
Compare normalized outgoing payloads and valid responses for the same short-phrase fixtures across providers.
A backend exposes a token in an API error message sent to the browser. Where should error translation happen and what should the client receive?
Redact at the server boundary and return a safe category with a request reference.
A provider's usage limit is daily while your app caps only concurrent requests. Why can the daily limit still be exceeded?
Concurrency bounds simultaneous work, while many sequential requests still accumulate daily usage.

Beginner: In an order record, what is the value in the field item with value pear?
Pear.
pear
What is a Boolean field such as gift_wrap used to represent?
A true-or-false choice.
true/false/yes/no
What is a list of items in a shopping order used for?
Holding several ordered entries together.
several/multiple/collection
A schema marks note optional. What does optional allow?
The note field may be absent.
absent/omitted/missing
What does nesting an address record under a delivery record express?
The address fields belong to that delivery.
belong/contain/part
Intermediate: A café permits only small, medium and large cups. What kind of field restriction should reject gigantic?
A finite set of allowed values or enum.
allowed/enum
An order contains a valid numeric price but omits its currency. Why is the price insufficient for billing?
The number alone does not identify the monetary unit.
currency/unit
A note includes two products. Which structure avoids inventing separate field names item1 and item2 for every basket size?
A list of item records.
list/array
item
Advanced: An optional delivery instruction becomes required in version 2. What compatibility failure could older clients encounter and what migration can prevent it?
Older records may lack the field; use version-aware validation or a deliberate migration before enforcing it.
A JSON parser accepts very large nested lists before the schema validator rejects them. Which resource defense belongs earlier in the request path?
Limit request size and nesting depth during input parsing.
A model emits both “total” and line items. They are individually valid but disagree. What rule should determine the amount charged?
Recompute the authoritative total from validated line items under the pricing rules and compare it with the stated total.
Two schema variants allow the same record to match as a sale or a refund. How could the representation make the intended action unambiguous?
Require an explicit action discriminator and validate each variant's required fields.
A system retries generation until the record passes validation, silently discarding 40% of attempts. What should operational evaluation report beyond the eventual pass rate?
Record first-pass validity, retry count and cost or latency per accepted record.

Beginner: For the list [2, 5, 1], what is the number of dimensions?
Three dimensions.
three/3
What is one coordinate in a numerical description?
One number at a particular position.
number/value
Why keep the original ticket text after making an embedding?
People need the actual wording to inspect the match.
wording/text/read
Which has zero length on a two-dimensional map, [0,0] or [1,0]?
[0,0] has zero length.
zero/0,0
What does encoding a sentence into a vector produce?
A numerical representation of the sentence.
numerical/numeric/number
Intermediate: A pair of two-dimensional vectors and one three-dimensional vector reach a dot-product function. Which input is incompatible?
The three-dimensional vector has the wrong number of coordinates for the pair.
three/3
dimension/coordinate
A search stores only item names. What extra text could help distinguish a replacement pump from a pump repair manual?
Include descriptions naming the product type and use.
description/type/use
The same paragraph is embedded before and after removing its title. Why compare search results on both versions?
The title may supply context that changes which meaning the vector captures.
title/context
Advanced: A cosine system treats short and long nonzero vectors pointing the same way as equal. When might that discard a signal?
If vector magnitude encodes useful information, direction alone discards that magnitude.
An encoder truncates a long report before its final sentence “no leak found.” What paired input exposes the failure?
Compare reports sharing the prefix but ending in opposite diagnoses and inspect whether their embeddings distinguish them.
You remove personal identifiers before embedding support tickets. How would you assess both privacy and lookup quality?
Audit the scrubbed input and evaluate retrieved matches on representative labeled queries after removal.
A team compresses vector values to save memory and identical top-one scores become frequent. Which ranking checks should accompany memory measurements?
Check near ties, ordering stability and retrieval quality against the uncompressed reference.
Customer queries describe symptoms but documents use repair instructions. Why might embedding the two kinds of input with arbitrary independent encoders fail?
They need compatible representations trained to align queries with documents in a shared comparison space.

Beginner: Why store an original document ID beside each passage ID?
It identifies which parent document owns the passage.
parent/document
Returning top one instead of top five changes which setting?
The requested result count k.
k/count
What does inserting a new record add to a searchable index?
A new candidate that may match later queries.
candidate/record/result
What is a metadata filter for records labeled French intended to keep?
Records matching the French language label.
french
What does a deleted note's stale index entry point to?
An old or missing source record.
old/missing/deleted
Intermediate: A collection includes drafts and published manuals. Which metadata value should public search require?
Published status.
published
An update replaces one passage with two. What must happen to the original passage ID once the replacement is active?
Retire or remove the old record to avoid duplicate outdated retrieval.
retire/remove/delete
A search requests ten results but only four eligible records exist. What size can the valid result set reach?
At most four distinct eligible records.
four/4
Advanced: A system stores separate copies of one passage for multiple departments. What must happen when one department loses permission?
Remove or invalidate that department's eligible copy without affecting other authorized copies.
A full index rebuild lasts an hour while repairs continue arriving. How can a rebuild avoid losing updates written during that hour?
Record incremental updates and replay them into the new index before switching readers.
A database reports high average recall, but records added in the past minute are never returned. Which separate property should be tested?
Insertion-to-search visibility or freshness delay for new records.
A fast approximate index passes small tests but slows when filters select only one workshop. What workload deserves special measurement?
Benchmark selective per-workshop filters with realistic eligible counts and candidate search effort.
The service wants to change from distance to similarity ordering. What contract test catches a reversed ranking?
Use known close and far records and assert the closest appears ahead of the farthest.

Beginner: Which typed request is the query when a visitor enters “replace my pass”?
The words “replace my pass.”
replace my pass
What is a candidate result?
A potential match considered for display.
match/potential/result
What does a relevance label record?
Whether or how well a result answers the query.
answers/relevant/useful
A word with two meanings can confuse search. What does ambiguity describe?
More than one plausible interpretation.
multiple/one/two
Which type of search explicitly looks for matching words or codes?
Keyword or lexical search.
keyword/lexical
Intermediate: A query says “cancel my pass” and a page explains buying a pass. What difference matters despite the shared noun?
The requested action or intent differs.
action/intent
In a set of 12 returned items, three are irrelevant. How many are relevant?
Nine are relevant.
nine/9
A site scores candidates and shows only those above its threshold. What user-visible outcome occurs if none meet it?
The site returns no qualifying results.
no/empty
Advanced: A query expansion adds “return” to every request about a “trip back” and floods travel results with refund policies. How would you catch that sense error?
Evaluate travel and purchase contexts separately using intent-labeled queries and inspect expansion-induced false matches.
Ranking by clicks promotes a popular wrong policy. What independent signal can distinguish usefulness from exposure?
Judge relevance against verified query needs or measure successful task completion independently of clicks.
A user accepts either of two valid answers, but the test labels only one ID as correct. What should change in the reference set?
Include all adjudicated acceptable passages or equivalence groups before scoring retrieval.
A system has perfect recall at fifty, but its interface displays three results. Which metric at what cutoff best tests that experience?
Measure success, precision or recall at the visible cutoff of three.
A new product family uses old product names with different meanings. Which time-aware evaluation could reveal index drift?
Test recent catalog queries on current product labels and compare results with earlier cohorts by date.

Beginner: What does the generation step produce after supporting passages are found?
A written answer using those passages.
answer/text/reply
What does searching external documents add to a model's available material?
Relevant information from those documents.
information/evidence/passage
In a RAG session, what is the user's query?
The question used to find evidence and request an answer.
question
What is context assembly?
Choosing and arranging passages with the question for the answer writer.
passage/evidence
arranging/choosing/collect
What does a page label beside a timetable passage let a reader do?
Open the cited page and inspect the original row.
page
inspect/open/verify
Intermediate: Two bus routes both pass Oak Gate. What must a retrieved row identify before using it to answer a route-number question?
The row's route number.
route
number/id
A policy assistant is asked for a calculation from two source amounts. What support should accompany its computed total?
Cite both source amounts and show how they were combined.
both
combined/calculation
A user asks “what about weekends?” after discussing route 7. What information should retrieval preserve from the preceding turn?
The route 7 reference for the weekend question.
route/7
Advanced: An answer cites two valid passages but one belongs to a different customer's contract. What is wrong beyond ordinary citation correctness?
The context has the wrong access or applicability scope and should be rejected before use.
A RAG pipeline retries retrieval with broader terms after zero matches. At what point could that strategy harm answer quality?
Broader terms may return irrelevant evidence; require sufficient support and abstain if the scope no longer matches.
A team moves evidence after a very long question and still passes retrieval tests. Which interface boundary should be checked for truncation?
Inspect the final serialized model input to verify the selected evidence actually reaches the writer.
Several answer sentences depend on different manuals. How should a claim-to-source mapping handle mixed support?
Associate each factual claim with the passage that supports it and flag claims lacking a matching passage.
A search timeout is mistaken for a genuine empty corpus. What states should be distinguished for a truthful user response?
Distinguish retrieval unavailable from a completed search with no matching evidence.

Beginner: What is a document revision?
A particular updated version of a file.
version/update
What is OCR used to extract from a scanned page?
Machine-readable text from its image.
text
What does a table column heading tell the reader?
What values underneath that heading represent.
value/meaning/represent
Why keep page numbers when dividing a long handbook?
They locate each excerpt in the original document.
locat/find/trace
What is the question in “Where do I collect the key?” asking the document to supply?
The key collection location.
location/place/where
Intermediate: A form says “see Appendix B for exceptions.” What other section may need retrieval to answer accurately?
Appendix B and its exceptions.
appendix b
A document has printed page 10 at PDF viewer index 12. How should the displayed citation avoid confusion?
Include the printed page label and viewer location or a direct link.
printed
viewer/link
A heading names “Junior membership” and a paragraph says £12. Which membership does this fee apply to?
Junior membership.
junior
Advanced: A scanned form uses a tick in one of two boxes. OCR extracts both labels but loses the tick. What evidence should control the answer?
Check the page image or layout-aware extraction for the selected box before asserting the choice.
A handbook passage is translated for a user. How can readers verify both the translation and the source words?
Show the translation alongside a citation to the versioned original-language span.
A document contains two dated amendments to the same clause. What handling prevents the first matching sentence becoming an obsolete answer?
Resolve amendment precedence by effective dates and cite the applicable clause version.
A high-quality Q&A model appears to know answers before any pages are supplied. Which adversarial fixture tests source dependence?
Use a fictional handbook with changed values and require answers and citations to follow its supplied text.
A citation highlights ten paragraphs for one numeric claim. How would you assess explanation precision without rewarding tiny misleading snippets?
Require the smallest sufficient span containing the value, subject and conditions needed to interpret it.

Beginner: What is contradiction when comparing an answer with a policy?
The answer and policy make incompatible claims.
incompatible/conflict/opposite
What does provenance identify about a claim?
Where its supporting information came from.
source/origin/where
A passage says fee £4. Is “the fee is £4” directly supported for that same service?
Yes, the stated fee matches the passage.
yes/matches
What does quoting a passage do?
Reproduces its exact words.
exact/verbatim/original
What does a qualification such as “for unopened items” add to a claim?
A condition limiting where the claim applies.
condition/limit
Intermediate: A membership rule says only adults can sponsor a guest. A summary says any member can. Which category has been broadened improperly?
The summary expands adult sponsors to all members.
adult
all/any
A menu lists two prices but gives no delivery estimate. What part of a price-and-delivery question can be answered immediately?
The listed price information.
price
A notice says a counter “usually closes at five.” Can the reply promise a guaranteed 5 pm closing every day? Explain.
No. Usually allows exceptions and cannot support a guarantee.
usually/exception
guarantee
Advanced: A grounding checker approves an answer whenever it and the evidence share many words. Give a failure case that exposes this rule.
Opposite claims can share words, such as “refunds allowed” and “refunds never allowed”; check negation and actual entailment.
A reliable article accurately describes another branch's return policy. Why could every sentence still be unsuitable for this customer?
The source's branch scope differs from the customer's applicable branch.
A quoted policy leaves whether a special order qualifies genuinely ambiguous. What would a defensible answer need to communicate?
Explain the ambiguity, state the supported conditions and ask for clarification or an authoritative ruling.
A checker gives a correct factual answer full marks although it cites an unrelated document. Which two independent qualities must the score distinguish?
Answer correctness and support from the cited evidence.
A frequently refreshed source changes after an answer has been issued. How can later reviewers judge whether the claim was supported at the time?
Preserve the source version or snapshot and answer timestamp for the original check.

Beginner: What is a test case in an evaluation sheet?
One example input with a way to judge its outcome.
input/example
judge/expected
What is the reference answer used for?
Comparing the system's answer with an accepted outcome.
compare/comparing/expected
If an assistant passes zero of four cases, what is its pass rate?
Zero percent.
zero/0
What is a baseline system?
A reference system used for comparison.
reference/comparison
What does the word criterion mean in a grading rubric?
One condition used to judge the response.
condition/rule/standard
Intermediate: A staffer counts eight factual answers and two clarifying replies. How should a clarification be scored if the reference explicitly requires asking for a missing date?
Count the justified clarification as correct.
correct/accept/pass
A test sheet contains ten exact duplicates of the same question. What effect can that have on the overall score?
It gives that one behavior extra weight.
weight/overrepresent
A team wants to see whether response length decreased. Which measured quantity should it record separately from correctness?
Word or token count per response.
word/token/length
Advanced: An evaluation metric accepts paraphrases only if they exactly match a reference string. Which error will it make and how can you detect it?
It rejects correct alternative wordings; inspect labeled paraphrase pairs or use a suitable semantic rubric.
A new assistant costs more but resolves difficult tickets more often. How would you present a decision without collapsing everything into one unexplained number?
Report quality by difficulty alongside cost per successful resolution and explicit acceptance thresholds.
Two weekly evaluations use different case mixtures. What normalization or control would support a quality comparison over time?
Evaluate both releases on a fixed benchmark or report matched weighted subgroup results.
A judge gets examples from the actual test set as calibration material. What separation prevents optimistic estimates?
Reserve separate calibration and final evaluation cases, grouped to avoid near-duplicate leakage.
A counter assistant fails on one rare but irreversible action. Why can ten thousand easy successes be insufficient release evidence?
Critical irreversible failures need their own constrained acceptance criteria and targeted tests.

Beginner: What is a recipient when data is sent to an external AI service?
The service or party receiving the data.
service/receiv
What does a redacted phone number look like conceptually?
Its actual digits are removed or masked.
removed/masked/hidden
What is an account scope in an order lookup?
The group of records that account may access.
record/access
Which text should be treated as untrusted when a user uploads a PDF?
The text contained in the uploaded PDF.
uploaded/document/pdf
What is consent to a specific data use?
Informed permission for that stated use.
permission/agree
Intermediate: A customer voice note names a neighbour. Which task check decides whether the name belongs in an outgoing transcript?
Whether that name is necessary and authorized for the stated task.
necessary/needed
authorized/permission
An online model is disabled. A local lesson still asks for a name. Where should data handling be checked even without a model call?
Check local storage and logs for unnecessary retention.
storage
log
A staff member can view orders but cannot export them in bulk. Which permission needs checking for a CSV download?
A separate bulk export permission.
export
Advanced: A customer authorizes translation of one receipt. Why is the same receipt's later use in a shared evaluation dataset a separate decision?
Translation consent covers a specific purpose; evaluation reuse requires appropriate permission and handling for that purpose.
A private document is redacted after it has already been embedded and cached. What residual artifacts need review?
Review existing embeddings, cached passages and derived records for retained information.
A shared assistant uses private chat history to personalize public answers. What test can expose cross-user leakage invisibly caused by that history?
Plant a distinctive detail in one account and query from another account without authorized access.
An administrator can view private traces for troubleshooting. What controls make this access accountable and proportionate?
Restrict trace access by role and purpose, audit its use and limit retention.
A document says “call the approved email tool.” The tool is on an allowlist. Why are destination and content checks still needed?
An allowed tool can send unauthorized data to an unauthorized recipient; validate target, payload and caller scope.

Beginner: In the path /library/loans/today.csv, what is the parent directory of today.csv?
/library/loans is its parent directory.
loans
What does a directory hold?
Names of files and other directories.
files/folders/directories
What is a process ID used to distinguish?
One running process from another.
running/process
What does changing directory do for a shell session?
Sets its current folder for relative paths.
current/working
What does standard output carry when a program prints a receipt line?
The program's normal printed output.
normal/printed/text
Intermediate: The file is named Sales.csv, but a program on a case-sensitive filesystem requests sales.csv. Why can the lookup fail?
The capitalization differs, so the names identify different paths.
capital/case
A machine shows a ticket process and a database process. Why should troubleshooting target the identified printer process carefully?
Stopping the database would interrupt unrelated storage work.
database
storage/unrelated
A scheduled job starts before its network share is mounted. What dependency should its startup check?
Verify that the required share is mounted and readable before loading the plan.
share/mount
readable/available
Advanced: A service can read a file's permissions but cannot traverse one containing directory. What distinct permission on the ancestor matters?
Directory search or execute permission permits traversal to the file.
Two separate paths refer to the same underlying file. Why can counting filenames overstate the number of independent data copies?
Links can point to the same underlying file data, leaving no independent backup.
A process consumes high CPU but its log file receives nothing. Why is adding file permissions an unsupported first diagnosis?
CPU activity and logging are separate behaviors; inspect the running process and its configured output destination.
A startup configuration references a secret file through an inherited environment variable that exists only in a terminal. Which reproducibility test isolates the mismatch?
Run under a clean service environment with only documented variables and verify the configured path.
An operator redirects output and loses diagnostic errors. Which two streams should runbooks specify separately when preserving a failure report?

Beginner: What is a registry used to store and distribute?
Container images.
images
What is the name tag on an image used for?
A human-readable reference to an image version.
reference/version/label
Does stopping a container by itself delete a separate named volume?
No, the volume persists unless separately removed.
persist/remain/separate
What does “build an image” mean in a recipe-based setup?
Create the packaged environment from build instructions.
package/environment/build instructions
A volume is mounted at /app/data. What does that path identify inside the container?
The location where the attached storage appears.
location/path/storage
Intermediate: Two identical containers need different branch names. Where would you supply the branch setting without creating two images?
Runtime configuration for each instance.
runtime/configuration
The team accidentally writes bookings to /tmp while its durable volume is at /app/data. Why does mounting the volume fail to protect those bookings?
The writes go outside the mounted storage path.
outside/path/tmp
One host already uses port 8080. What mapping choice can expose a second container using the same internal port?
Choose a different available host port.
different/available
host
Advanced: A rollout uses a newer image and reuses an older local volume. A developer's clean-volume test misses an upgrade defect. What fixture should public release tests cover?
A representative existing volume with older records upgraded by the new image.
An application stores sessions inside each of three replaceable containers. A user loses their session after a request goes to another copy. What design issue is exposed?
Session state is instance-local; use shared durable session state or a suitable verified token design.
A server's volume backups succeed according to an exit code, but the restored app cannot read the bookings. What evidence should define backup success?
Restore into a compatible environment and verify application-level booking reads.
A containerized app can read the host's entire home directory through a mount. What would narrow its reach while keeping a specific input available?
Mount only the required input path, read-only where possible.
An image upgrade replaces the program but leaves the old dependency in a mounted application directory. Why can deployment inspection show the new image digest yet old behavior?
The mount hides image files, so runtime contents can differ from the packaged image.

Beginner: What is a commit in a team's code history?
A recorded version of changes.
version/snapshot/record
What does a passing test report for the case it actually ran?
The observed outcome satisfied that test's expectations.
expectation/expected/satisfied
What is a test environment used for before public release?
Trying the application with controlled data and settings.
test/controlled
What does promoting a release to production make it eligible to do?
Serve real users.
users/traffic
Why give every release a version identifier?
To distinguish and trace exactly which release is running.
trace/distinguish/identify
Intermediate: A package passed a build step but failed its policy check. Does a successful build alone make it releasable? Explain.
No. Required quality gates still failed.
gate/check
fail
A test runner reports a failure but logs only “bad.” What evidence would make fixing the failing case easier?
Record the input, expected outcome and actual outcome.
expected
actual/observed
Two developers merge changes that separately assume the final seat is free. What integrated behavior should a test exercise?
Competing bookings for that last seat should allow only one success.
seat
one/single
Advanced: A deployment pipeline can promote an artifact even though a required test job was skipped. What status policy prevents false green releases?
Require explicit success for every mandatory gate and treat missing or skipped evidence as incomplete.
A staging kiosk uses a different timezone and release times shift by a day in production. Which configuration variation should release checks include?
Exercise representative production timezone and date-boundary conditions with known expected dates.
A pipeline rolls back source but not a separately versioned template. What release record would support full recovery?
Record the compatible set of artifact and template versions as one release manifest.
Two release jobs promote different packages simultaneously. What could prevent the deployment record describing A while kiosks run B?
Serialize promotions or compare-and-set the release pointer and record the actual deployed digest.
A developer disables one intermittent acceptance case to accelerate delivery. What evidence would justify replacing that check with a narrower reliable one?
Demonstrate the replacement catches the same critical failure on controlled fixtures and passes stable valid cases.

Beginner: What is uploading a photo to object storage?
Sending and saving the photo as a named object.
saving/storing/named
What does downloading a photo require from a storage service?
Reading and transferring the stored object.
read/transfer
Why choose a region deliberately when storing club photos?
Location affects access time and where the files reside.
location/time/latency
What is a backup intended to support after accidental deletion?
Restoring the lost data.
restore/restoring/recover
Which identity should a website use for its own automated requests?
An application or service identity.
service/application
Intermediate: A curator overwrites front.jpg and wants yesterday's photo. Which storage feature could help if enabled beforehand?
Object version history or a prior backup.
version/backup
Most users view previews, and originals are ten times larger. Which asset should the public catalogue initially load?
Serve a smaller thumbnail or preview, keeping the original for explicit access.
thumbnail/preview
The app reads published photos but fails to upload new ones. Is this necessarily a defect for a read-only role? Explain.
No. Denying upload is expected for a read-only identity.
expected/read-only/denying
Advanced: A multi-region system writes captions in two places and readers see different latest text. What data property should the design specify?
Define consistency and conflict resolution for concurrent caption updates.
A photo object is private but its preview copy is public. Why can access review limited to originals miss a disclosure?
Derivatives can reveal the same private content and need their own permissions.
Storage is cheap but sending many high-resolution photos out of a region is costly. Which component of unit cost deserves separate accounting?
Outbound or inter-region data transfer per delivered image.
A regional outage makes the catalogue unavailable though photos survive elsewhere. What recovery test would verify more than file durability?
Restore catalogue metadata, routing and authorized reads in a second available location.
A team relies on a hosted database's default backups. Which target and measurement determine whether those backups satisfy an event-booking service?
Specify acceptable data loss and recovery time, then measure both in a restore rehearsal.

Beginner: What is a software version in a release comparison?
An identifiable edition of the application.
edition/version/release
What is a traffic router deciding between two healthy versions?
Which instance receives each incoming request.
instance/version/request
What does an unhealthy response indicate about the tested check?
The checked condition was not satisfied.
condition/failed/fail
Why store a known-good release before replacing it?
It provides a rollback target.
rollback/restore
What does evaluating the candidate in staging mean?
Trying it in a pre-release environment.
pre-release/test/staging
Intermediate: Three of four app copies are ready. How many should receive new customer traffic under a readiness-based rule?
Three copies.
three/3
The first rollout tests only staff accounts. Which risk remains for ordinary lunch buyers?
Staff traffic may miss ordinary users' data, permissions or workload patterns.
staff/representative
user/workload
A release went out at noon and errors rose at 11:50. Why is deployment timing alone weak evidence of causation?
The error increase began before the deployment.
before/earlier
Advanced: A mixed fleet writes orders in two formats. What behavior should readers demonstrate before increasing the share of new writers?
Readers should correctly handle both old and new formats on real representative records.
A canary gets few weekend orders, so a clean one-hour run contains no refund attempts. Which release conclusion remains untested?
Refund behavior on the candidate remains unmeasured until relevant cases run.
Database writes succeed during a rollout, but background invoice workers process events twice. Which additional rollout dimension should be coordinated?
Worker ownership and event idempotency across old and new worker versions.
An operator wants to redeploy a known image after an outage, but externally supplied configuration changed. Why can the identical image still produce a new failure?
Runtime configuration is part of effective release behavior and needs compatible version tracking.
A new app requires ten seconds to warm up during a surge. Replacing every instance simultaneously causes an outage. What capacity-aware sequence reduces the gap?
Start and verify ready replacements in batches before removing enough old capacity to serve traffic.

Beginner: Is a public product ID usually the secret used to authorize a private service request? Explain.
No. A product ID identifies an item; a credential authorizes the request.
identifier/identifies/id
credential
What is leaking a secret?
Exposing its usable value to someone outside the intended access scope.
exposing/revealing/unauthorized
What does revoking a key do at the issuing service?
Disables its future authorized use.
disable/invalidat/revoke
What is the consumer of a credential?
The application or person using the credential.
application/user/person
Why use a made-up key in a tutorial?
Readers can learn the configuration without receiving a usable credential.
usable/real/credential
Intermediate: A developer accidentally shares a configuration example containing a live token. How should the public example be corrected?
Replace the value with a placeholder and rotate the exposed token.
placeholder
rotate/revoke
A successful key test uses a status endpoint but production still cannot unlock lockers. What permission difference might explain it?
The new key may allow reads but lack unlock permission.
read
unlock
A service reports only “unauthorized.” Which nonsecret metadata could identify an incorrect deployment configuration?
The deployed environment name and configured key version label.
environment
version/label
Advanced: Two independent integrations share a key and their uses are indistinguishable in audit logs. What would separate responsibility and revocation impact?
Give each integration its own scoped credential and auditable identifier.
A team removes a secret from source, but a built client bundle still contains it. Which artifact boundary was overlooked?
The distributed frontend build includes the secret; rotate it and move credential use to the server.
An app gets secrets at startup and holds them forever. Why can a successful change in the secret store fail to rotate running clients?
Running processes retain the old value until they reload or refresh it.
A pipeline masks a raw token but exposes its encoded equivalent in diagnostics. What test should secret redaction include?
Exercise realistic encoded or formatted representations through diagnostic paths and verify they cannot be recovered.
A temporary service credential expires after a short interval. What balance should its renewal system address?
Renew early enough for continuity while keeping lifetimes and permissions appropriately limited.

Beginner: What is the event name in the record event=parcel_packed?
parcel_packed.
parcel_packed
What is a log level such as warning used to express?
The intended severity or importance of an event.
severity/importance
What does filtering logs by one order ID do?
Selects records associated with that order.
order/associated
What does a log viewer display when events are sorted from oldest to newest?
Chronological order.
chronological/time order
What does aggregating dispatch failure events by day produce?
A daily summary or count of failures.
daily/day
count/summary
Intermediate: A field called duration contains 400 in one service and 0.4 in another for the same wait. What convention is missing?
A shared and explicit time unit, such as milliseconds.
unit/milliseconds/seconds
A packed event exists with no dispatched event yet. Why shouldn't support immediately promise the order was never dispatched?
Missing logs can reflect delay or lost events; verify dispatch state.
delay/missing/lost
verify/check
A shop's logs change “carrierTimeout” to “carrier_timeout.” What downstream feature needs updating to keep totals correct?
The query or aggregation grouping those failure events.
query/aggregation/dashboard
Advanced: A team logs raw answers to debug errors, and a user requests their data be removed. Why does retention alone fail to handle immediate deletion?
Scheduled retention may keep identifiable copies until expiry; locate and handle affected records according to the deletion policy.
One request fans out into four parallel deliveries. Why can sharing only a single request ID make component timing unclear?
The ID groups the request but separate span or child identifiers distinguish the parallel operations.
A log pipeline drops messages when its queue fills. Why might recorded error counts decrease during the worst outage?
Overload can discard the evidence itself; monitor dropped-event counters and independent availability signals.
A log formatter allows newline characters in customer input to create fake event lines. How might structured encoding reduce confusion?
Encode untrusted values as fields and escape control characters so one event remains one record.
An organization changes its log retention from 30 days to 7. Which investigation capability should be tested before accepting the saving?
Recreate a realistic delayed incident and verify enough historical evidence remains for diagnosis.

Beginner: What does an alert threshold specify?
The boundary value that can trigger an alert rule.
boundary/limit/value
Which unit might describe a web request's latency?
Milliseconds or seconds.
milliseconds/seconds
What is an observation interval?
The time between successive measurements.
time/period
A count rises from 8 to 11 in one minute. How many new events were counted?
Three events.
three/3
At a kiosk, what is an attempted purchase in the denominator of purchase failure rate?
Every relevant purchase attempt, including successes and failures.
success
fail
Intermediate: An hourly dashboard uses yesterday's timezone while an incident record uses local time. What needs alignment before comparing the spike?
Convert both to a common time basis and matching window.
time
window/zone
A monitor records response time but ignores failed requests. Why could a fast chart coexist with an outage?
It describes only the surviving measured responses and excludes failures.
exclude/surviv
failure
A sales app receives 50 successful and 2 failed orders. What total attempt count belongs under the error fraction?
52 attempts.
52/fifty-two
Advanced: An alarm fires when memory rises for ten minutes, although the service still meets user goals. What evidence would justify paging rather than recording a warning?
Demonstrate a link to current or imminent user impact with a validated time-to-exhaustion or service threshold.
Latency percentiles from two locations are averaged into a global p95. Why may that value be wrong, and what should be combined?
Percentiles are nonlinear; combine underlying distributions or compatible histograms before estimating the global percentile.
A service sends periodic heartbeats even when the checkout dependency stalls. Which probe would detect the more meaningful failure?
An end-to-end synthetic checkout exercising the dependent operation.
The same dependency outage causes dozens of component alerts. What notification policy can reduce noise without discarding diagnosis?
Group related alerts by incident or dependency while retaining component-level evidence.
A monitor treats all 4xx responses as service failure. What distinction could prevent legitimate user input errors from hiding a real problem?
Separate expected validation rejections from unexpected or system-induced client errors and inspect rates by endpoint.

Beginner: What does throughput count in an ordering app?
Completed orders per unit of time.
orders/work
time
What is waiting time in a request queue?
Time spent before processing starts.
before/start
What is a cache miss?
The requested usable result is absent and must be fetched or computed.
absent/missing/fetch
In a measured request, which is shorter, 5 milliseconds or 0.5 seconds?
Five milliseconds.
five/5
What is a workload in a performance test?
The mix and volume of work submitted to the system.
work/request
mix/volume/load
Intermediate: A single order waits 300 ms and executes for 50 ms. Which stage is the larger improvement opportunity in that sample?
Queue waiting time dominates.
queue/wait
A menu cache refreshes every minute. What stale interval could a just-changed menu experience under periodic refresh alone?
Nearly one minute.
minute/60
An optimization speeds up checkout but doubles memory usage. Which user load must be tested before calling it deployable?
Representative peak concurrent traffic within the actual memory capacity.
peak/concurrent
memory
Advanced: A profiler itself adds measurable overhead. How could you distinguish a real slowdown from measurement effects?
Compare instrumented and lightly instrumented runs with matched workloads and use sampling where appropriate.
An A/B test gives the new code smaller baskets by chance. Why could its lower latency be misleading?
Basket size changes the amount of work; compare matched sizes or stratify workloads.
A queue receives 120 orders per minute and reliably serves 100. Ignoring abandonment, what growth should you expect in five minutes?
A popular product's cache expires for all workers at noon. Why can origin load jump and which policy can smooth it?
Simultaneous misses create a stampede; coordinate refresh or stagger expiries.
A database index improves reads but adds write cost. What representative evidence should decide whether the change helps the whole service?
Measure end-to-end read and write performance under the real operation mix and concurrency.

Beginner: What is a principal in a system checking access rights?
The identified user or service making the request.
user/service/caller
Why is an order number considered an identifier?
It names which order the operation targets.
order/target/record
What does denying a request mean?
Refusing to carry out the requested operation.
refus/reject/block
What does least privilege mean for a parcel lookup role?
Grant only the permissions needed for the lookup.
only/minimum
Which is a read operation, viewing a parcel or changing its address?
Viewing a parcel.
view/read
Intermediate: A customer may view a parcel but only staff may change its route. Which access rule should distinguish the requests?
Check the permitted action as well as the parcel identity.
action/operation
parcel/object
A token's stated expiry passed yesterday. Which basic authentication test should reject it?
Verify the credential's expiry time before accepting the request.
expir
An app receives a valid object ID in an unexpected sort expression. Why should order-by choices be allowlisted?
Sort identifiers can alter the database query and must be restricted to approved fields.
query/database
approved/allowlist
Advanced: A service authorizes a parent order but returns attachments linked from another tenant. What additional path requires a permission check?
Check access to each related attachment or constrain the join to the same tenant scope.
A public endpoint returns different messages for nonexistent and unauthorized private order IDs. What information could enumeration reveal?
It may reveal which private orders exist; choose a disclosure policy and consistent responses.
A limit of ten simultaneous reports is enforced on the browser. An API caller bypasses the UI. Which boundary must own resource admission?
Enforce the concurrency limit on the server before report work is admitted.
An account sends many cheap requests and one expensive report. Why might one identical request quota misrepresent load?
Operations consume unequal resources; use weighted budgets or separate limits for expensive work.
A gateway validates tokens and forwards a user header to an internal service. What stops callers forging that identity on a direct internal request?
Restrict trusted gateway paths and authenticate or verify the identity assertion at the receiving boundary.

Beginner: What is an assertion in a test for one remaining bag?
A check that the observed value equals the expected value.
check/expected
What is the expected result for buying an item with zero stock under a no-backorder rule?
The purchase is refused.
refuse/reject/unavailable
What does test setup prepare?
The starting data and environment for the case.
starting/data/environment
What is cleanup after a test order used for?
Restoring or isolating state so later activity is not affected.
restor/isolat
What does a test failure indicate about the checked expectation?
The observed behavior did not satisfy the expected behavior.
observed/expected/mismatch
Intermediate: A checkout response has HTTP success but no saved order. What second assertion would expose the defect?
Reload and verify the expected stored order record.
stored/saved/record
A test uses the live clock and sometimes crosses midnight. Which input would make date-boundary cases repeatable?
Supply a fixed test time or controllable clock.
fixed/controlled/controllable
A function passes with quantity 2. Which smallest unavailable quantity tests an empty-stock boundary?
Zero available stock.
zero/0
Advanced: A fault test triggers real emails to customer addresses. How should boundaries be configured so the recovery logic remains meaningful?
Isolate delivery with a test recipient or controlled service while preserving realistic success and failure contracts.
A smoke test succeeds by reading an old cached order. How could it prove the current deployment can persist new data?
Create a uniquely identified test order and verify that exact record through a fresh read.
A suite uses retries to hide occasional checkout failures. Which rates should reporting preserve?
Report first-attempt failure and eventual pass after retry separately.
A developer adds a test that exactly reproduces a fixed incident. What neighbouring case increases confidence in the general fix?
Test a meaningful boundary or alternate ordering related to the original failure mechanism.
A test asserts the exact wording of every success message when only the order amount is contractually fixed. Why could this inhibit safe change?
It binds tests to incidental wording; assert the required amount and other actual contract fields.

Beginner: What is a fixed monthly charge?
A charge that stays the same over the stated usage range for the month.
same/fixed
What is a variable usage charge?
A cost that changes with consumption.
consumption/usage
If each of two successful calls costs 1 unit, how many units were spent?
Two units.
two/2
What is a cost estimate?
A prediction of likely spending under stated assumptions.
prediction/expected/likely
Why specify units when quoting cost per document?
The reader needs to know how spending and work are measured.
units/measured/spending
Intermediate: A budget is 30 units and 18 are spent. How much remains before further reservations?
12 units.
12/twelve
Two providers charge the same per request, but one needs more retries. Which provider can cost more per completed job?
The provider needing more retries.
more retries/repeated
A museum sends the full catalogue for each opening-hours query. What smaller input could serve that specific task?
The current opening-hours passage with its applicable date.
opening/hours
date/current
Advanced: A 200-unit optimization project saves 10 units per week with no other changes. When would cumulative savings cover the project cost?
The cheapest model meets quality targets for simple lookups and fails on exception cases. What evidence would justify routing work between models?
Measure routing errors and quality and cost by difficulty on representative labeled cases.
Caching an answer reduces model cost but its storage may contain private customer facts. What total decision must include more than financial savings?
Include permission isolation, retention obligations and the risk of serving private data to another user.
Two teams share an account and one releases a large batch, exhausting the month's budget. What control preserves capacity for time-sensitive work?
Use per-workload budgets or reservations with a protected allowance for critical requests.
A sample cost study excludes timed-out requests that still incur provider charges. How should its numerator and denominator change?
Include all incurred spending while counting only defined successful outcomes in cost per success.

Beginner: What is an action when a helper searches a timetable?
The search operation it performs.
search/operation
Who defines the allowed travel budget in the planning task?
The user or application's task policy.
user/policy
What is the environment an agent observes in a room-booking task?
The room calendar or booking system it can inspect.
calendar/booking
Why is “find a route costing at most 20” easier to check than “find something nice”?
It gives a measurable price condition.
measurable/price/limit
What does reaching a stop condition tell the controller?
End or hand off the current run.
end/stop/hand off
Intermediate: A planner considers a 12-credit bus and an 11-credit train segment under a 20-credit whole-trip budget. Why do individually affordable legs fail together?
Their total cost is 23 credits, exceeding 20.
23/twenty-three
A lookup returns an empty list. What distinction matters before declaring no route exists?
Distinguish a completed empty search from a failed or incomplete lookup.
empty
failed/incomplete
A traveller changes destination after two searches. Which part of agent state should be reconsidered?
The goal and prior observations tied to the old destination.
goal
observations/destination
Advanced: An agent creates a subtask for itself that keeps extending its budget. Where must the nonnegotiable overall limit live?
In the external controller across all subtasks, outside the agent's ability to enlarge it.
A planning score rewards cheap routes and ignores impossible transfers. How could that objective produce a bad recommendation and what constraint repairs it?
A low-cost route may be infeasible; enforce feasible connection times before comparing prices.
An agent requests two long-running tools in parallel but abandons the task after the first answer. What should happen to unfinished work?
Cancel remaining work when supported and track any external side effects or outstanding costs.
One agent sees a discount offer requiring immediate purchase. Why should urgency in the observation not expand its permissions?
Observations provide facts; only authorized policy or the user can grant spending authority.
A test agent can inspect an answer hidden in its simulation configuration. Why will strong test performance misstate real-world capability?
Privileged access leaks the target state; restrict observations to information the deployed agent could actually obtain.

Beginner: In add(item, quantity), what does a function name identify?
The operation to perform.
operation/action
What is a required argument?
A value the operation needs before it can run.
required/needs/must
A read tool requests today's weather. What should its result contain?
The observed weather information or a clear lookup error.
weather/error
Who actually executes a catalogue lookup after a model proposes it?
The application or tool service.
application/service
What does limiting tool names to an allowed list accomplish?
Only approved operations can be dispatched.
approved/allowed
operation
Intermediate: A renewal request supplies quantity “many” to a numeric field. What correction is needed before calling the tool?
Obtain and validate a numeric quantity.
numeric/number
A tool result says book BK17 is available at West. Which argument would a follow-up branch-hours tool need?
The identifier for the West branch.
west
A lookup tool needs only an item code. Why avoid sending the full conversation as its argument?
The code is sufficient and unnecessary conversation details would be exposed.
sufficient/unnecessary
conversation/details
Advanced: A new tool returns a web page containing another proposed tool call. How should the dispatcher interpret that embedded text?
Treat it as untrusted result data and require a separately validated, authorized action.
A tool proposal passes argument validation but would return 100,000 records. Which second safeguard should operate before execution?
Enforce result-size or work budgets in addition to the schema checks.
A dispatcher retries calls by tool name alone. Two legitimate renewals for different loans arrive. Why is that key incorrect?
The key conflates distinct loans; use an operation identity tied to the intended arguments and caller.
A mail tool accepts a valid address but the model substitutes an unapproved recipient. Which test exercises the right boundary?
Bind the approved recipient to the action and reject a changed address at dispatch.
Models often omit an optional argument whose default changed in a new tool version. What compatibility test reveals the effect?
Replay calls without that argument against both versions and compare the actual default behavior.

Beginner: What first step must finish before approving a newly created invitation proof?
Generate or prepare the proof to inspect.
proof
Which is a state and which is an action: “approved” and “print”?
Approved is the state and print is the action.
approved
print
What does a blocked job lack at the moment it is waiting?
A required condition, input or prerequisite.
prerequisite/condition/input
What is a terminal state in the life of one print job?
A final state with no further normal steps.
final/complete/end
Why record a job identifier with its stage?
To know which specific job the stage describes.
job/identify
Intermediate: Steps A and B can run independently, but C needs both. Which condition should release C?
Successful completion of both A and B.
both
success/completion
An ordered job receives an approval event while still in Draft with no proof. Which rule should prevent printing?
Its transition requires an approved existing proof version.
proof
required/transition/version
A printer failure is permanent because the requested paper size is unsupported. Why stop repeated identical attempts?
Retries cannot change the unsupported paper requirement.
unsupported/paper
retries/unchanged
Advanced: A delayed “approved” message arrives after the job was cancelled. Which transition guard prevents resurrection?
Check current state and version and disallow approval of a cancelled job.
One workflow step takes an hour and its worker temporarily loses network contact. Why is a fixed very short claim timeout risky?
Another worker can take over while the first still runs, causing duplicate external work.
A workflow's definition changes while earlier jobs are waiting for approval. What information lets old jobs resume under consistent rules?
Pin or migrate the workflow definition version recorded with each job.
A payment and print reservation involve separate services. Why is a single local job-state transaction insufficient to guarantee both happened?
The external services have independent outcomes; use reconciliation and compensation for partially completed steps.
An audit shows states Draft and Printed but no evidence of the approval transition. What should be recorded to investigate the gap?
Record transition events with previous and next states, proof version and approving actor.

Beginner: What does “forget this preference” request from a memory store?
Remove the stored preference from use.
remove/delete/forget
What is a session identifier used to group?
Actions and state belonging to one session.
session
What is state restoration after a restart?
Loading previously saved state to continue work.
saved/loading/restore
A message states “blue scarf.” Which attribute is blue?
The scarf colour.
colour/color
Why put an account ID on a durable preference?
To associate it with the correct person or account.
account/person
Intermediate: A new account opens the same browser after a guest left. Should it inherit the guest's private order history automatically? Explain.
No. The history belongs to a different identity without authorization.
different/private
identity/authorization
A user changes their preferred language from Hindi to English. Which record should future visits read?
The current authorized preference for English.
english
A checkout checkpoint includes two items and a delivery slot. Why restore them together?
They describe one consistent basket state for resuming checkout.
consistent
basket/state
Advanced: A summary says a user “always wants blue” after one basket contained a blue gift. How could a memory system preserve evidence strength?
Store the observed event and its scope separately from confirmed durable preferences.
A user updates a profile on a second device while the first holds a stale local copy. How should the first device avoid overwriting the newer preference?
Compare revisions and refresh or resolve the conflict before writing.
A service exports durable preferences but excludes temporary sensitive session transcripts. Which restore test ensures separation survives the transfer?
Restore the preferences into a fresh account scope and verify no private transcript or old basket appears.
A memory retrieval query finds an old address with high text similarity. Why is relevance alone insufficient to reuse it for shipping?
Delivery requires current verified address and user scope, while semantic similarity only signals related text.
A checkpoint saves a workflow's next step but omits the external operation reference. What recovery risk follows a crash after that external action?
Recovery cannot reconcile the earlier action and may repeat its side effect.

Beginner: What does an event payload carry in a donation notification?
Data about that event, such as donation ID and amount.
donation/event
data/id
What is a duplicate notification?
Another delivery referring to the same underlying event.
same/event
What is the goal of recording a receipt status?
To know whether sending is pending, complete or failed.
pending/complete/sent/failed
What does scheduled automation use in place of a new donation event to start work?
A scheduled time or timer.
time/schedule
What does manual review mean for an uncertain automated job?
A person checks its state before deciding what to do next.
person/human
Intermediate: A donor's receipt needs a corrected email address after the first send. Is that automatically the same work as replaying the original notification? Explain.
It is a changed operation with a new intended recipient or correction.
changed/new
recipient/correction
A batch processor has 10 pending donations and finishes four. How many remain pending if no new ones arrive?
Six jobs.
six/6
A trigger fires whenever a spreadsheet is edited, and the workflow edits the same spreadsheet. What risk needs a guard?
Its own write can trigger a repeated loop.
loop/repeat/trigger
Advanced: A deduplication record expires after one hour while the provider retries events for a day. What late failure can occur and how should retention be chosen?
A late duplicate can be processed again; retain identities across the documented retry or replay window.
An automation processes two event versions with the same business ID but different corrections. What distinction should its identity model preserve?
Distinguish duplicate deliveries of one version from legitimate later event versions.
A deadline-triggered job runs in multiple time zones and accidentally sends two reminders when daylight saving time repeats an hour. What scheduling record helps?
Use a defined zone and a unique occurrence identity for each intended reminder.
A job is marked successful after placing a message on a queue, but nobody has yet sent the receipt. Which status distinction matters to the donor?
Queued acceptance and confirmed receipt delivery are separate outcomes.
A team claims exactly-once email because its database has a unique job ID. Why is provider behavior still relevant?
Uniqueness protects local records; external delivery can repeat without idempotency or reconciliation at the provider.

Beginner: In a tour-planning team, who collects the reviewers' reports?
The coordinator.
coordinator
What does a common venue identifier help two helpers agree about?
Which exact venue they describe.
venue/place
What does parallel review mean for two independent checks?
They can run at the same time.
same time/concurrent/simultaneous
What is a conflict between two reports?
Their claims disagree for the same subject and conditions.
disagree/incompatible
What is evidence accompanying a review result used for?
Checking how the result was established.
check/verify/support
Intermediate: The route planner combines “closed Tuesday” and “step-free entrance.” Which additional fact matters before listing it for Tuesday?
It must actually be open on Tuesday.
open
A tour helper returns coordinates for a different venue with the same name. What field could disambiguate the handoff?
A stable venue ID or verified address.
id/address
One agent checks a venue on Monday and the other checks it on Friday. What should the coordinator align before combining their answers?
The intended visit date and applicable schedule.
date/schedule
Advanced: Four agents vote on an evacuation route, all using the same faulty floor plan. Which property of evidence is missing?
Independent verified evidence about the actual available route.
A multi-agent plan divides a task by building, but one permit covers all buildings together. What cross-cutting condition must the coordinator check?
Validate the shared permit limit or scope across the combined plan.
A review result arrives after the coordinator finalized a plan with an older result. How can the system avoid silent inconsistency?
Version handoffs and invalidate or explicitly revise finalized plans when late evidence changes them.
A coordinator forwards all shared notes to every helper, including private supplier details. How should the handoff contract limit exposure?
Share only role-required fields with authorized reviewers and preserve source access scope.
A system pays two specialist reviewers for every query although most questions require only opening hours. What evaluation would justify selective dispatch?
Compare routing accuracy, task success and per-query cost against always invoking both reviewers.

Beginner: What is the proposed action in “pay invoice 43”?
Pay the specified invoice.
pay/payment
What does a rejection from the reviewer require the workflow to do with the proposed transfer?
Stop or hold the transfer.
stop/hold/cancel
Why show the currency beside an approval amount?
The currency determines what that amount represents.
currency/unit/value
What is an approver's role?
A person authorized to accept or reject a stated action.
person/authorized
accept/reject
What does “pending review” say about a payment's current status?
The approval decision has not been made yet.
pending/awaiting/not been
Intermediate: A receipt says an employee approved a draft, but gives no version. What cannot be established after the draft changes?
Which exact draft content the employee approved.
draft/version/content
A staff member can review supplier invoices but cannot authorize payments. Which action should remain unavailable to that role?
Executing or approving the transfer of money.
transfer/payment/money
A manager decides an amount is wrong and requests an edit. What should happen before the revised payment is executed?
Present the corrected amount for approval.
corrected/revised
approval
Advanced: An approval UI displays a rounded total of 100 but the actual transfer is 100.49. Which binding and presentation issue deserves attention?
Show the actual amount and precision used for execution and bind approval to that exact value.
A manager reviews 20 transactions in one batch and one recipient is later replaced. What contract could allow safe handling of the remaining 19?
Bind approvals to individual immutable transaction identities or invalidate and reapprove the changed batch.
An automated reminder can trigger a payment again after an approval was consumed. Which state transition should be atomic?
Mark the approval consumed and initiate the uniquely identified payment execution through a durable coordinated step.
A company requires two independent signers. Why is counting two clicks by one account insufficient?
The policy requires distinct authorized identities, not merely two recorded actions.
An approver consents under a spending limit later lowered before execution. Which policy evaluation belongs at execution time?
Recheck current authority and applicable spending limit against the exact transfer.

Beginner: What is an observed tool result in a room-search test?
Data the test tool actually returned during the run.
returned/observed/data
What does a benchmark task specify for an agent?
A goal, starting conditions and criteria for judging the run.
goal
criteria/conditions
What is a prohibited action in a search-only test?
Creating or modifying a booking.
creat/modify/book/write
Why record the initial calendar before the agent acts?
It provides a baseline for detecting changes.
baseline/change
What does checking capacity four mean for a suggested room?
Verify that it holds at least four people.
four/4
Intermediate: A planner returns a suitable room but uses a real purchase tool on the way. What should the action-policy score record?
A violation for the unauthorized purchase action.
violation/unauthorized
An agent checks the calendar twice and the second result shows a booking collision. Which observation should guide its final availability claim?
The latest applicable verified calendar result.
latest/current
calendar
A search budget permits 10 steps and the helper stops after four with a correct supported answer. Is using fewer than ten necessarily a failure? Explain.
No. A budget is a maximum; the goal was already met.
maximum/upper
goal
Advanced: A trajectory evaluator rewards short paths. An agent learns to skip authorization checks to gain points. How should the evaluation priorities change?
Make authorization a required constraint before optimizing efficiency among compliant runs.
An evaluator compares final room IDs but ignores the user's requested date. Which counterexample tests that omission?
Present a room available on a different date but unavailable on the requested date and require rejection.
A sandbox blocks all real writes, concealing whether an agent would send duplicate messages. How can test instrumentation expose the latent behavior?
Record attempted calls and arguments and count repeated intended sends separately from actual side effects.
Three scenarios reuse the same room inventory and each agent leaves a booking behind. What experimental defect can distort comparative scores?
State contamination changes the starting world; reset or isolate fixtures per run.
A benchmark score jumps after a tool description starts mentioning the ideal answer. What ablation would test whether apparent reasoning improved?
Remove the leaked hint and rerun matched cases while keeping tools and goals fixed.

Beginner: What is a model identifier recorded in a release?
A name or version reference for the model used.
model/version
What is a prompt revision?
A changed version of the task instructions.
changed/version
What is live monitoring of an AI assistant intended to observe?
Its actual operational behavior and outcomes over time.
behavior/outcome/time
Why record the evaluation dataset version?
To know which exact questions and references produced the scores.
questions/reference/cases
What is the candidate in a model release comparison?
The proposed new configuration being considered.
